title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
abstract: arXiv:2611.03223v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not identify where each violation comes from. We introduce ARCBench(Agent Rule Compliance Benchmark), a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness. Its tool-calling agent loop lets us measure rule compliance from actions taken during execution, bringing the evaluation closer to deployed agent workflows. Using ARCBench, we examine where violations after compaction come from, and how different compaction configurations and adversarial settings change their sources. We find that compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as pe

translated_title: 智能体还会遵守规则吗？在智能体上下文压缩下的规则遵守基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体会压缩长历史记录以适应其上下文窗口，但压缩后的上下文仍必须承载约束后续操作的运行规则。先前的研究表明压缩后违规行为会增加，但这些工作在完整的智能体框架之外测量合规性，且未能识别每项违规的具体来源。我们提出了 ARCBench（智能体规则合规基准），这是一个构建于开源 pi 智能体框架之上的可配置基准测试。其基于工具调用的智能体循环使我们能够从执行期间采取的实际动作中测量规则合规性，使评估更贴近实际部署的智能体工作流。借助 ARCBench，我们研究了压缩后违规行为的来源，以及不同的压缩配置和对抗性设置如何改变这些来源。我们发现压缩很少会删除规则本身：压缩后的大多数违规行为发生在规则仍然存在于压缩历史中的情况下，此时智能体将后续请求视为…（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 提出 ARCBench 基准，在完整智能体框架中通过实际执行动作测量上下文压缩后的规则遵守情况，并发现压缩后的大多数违规并非因为规则被删除，而是在规则仍保留于压缩历史中时智能体对后续请求处理不当所致。
en_tdlr: Introduces ARCBench, a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness that measures rule compliance from actual executed actions within a complete agent loop, finding that most post-compaction violations occur while the rule is still present in the compacted history rather than because the rule was deleted.
